# Population prior on the lesion split, fitted to PSST

Fitted on the 74 training-split participants' BNT errors (339 codable, 224 of their rows clinician-adjudicated), by multinomial likelihood of the five SP error types under the cohort's pooled expected response probabilities. Grid: log p/s mean -1.5 to 1.0 by 0.1, sd in [0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0].

**Chosen: log p/s mean -0.2, sd 0.3.** Deviance against the saturated model 164.8 on 4 degrees of freedom; Dell's prior (mean +0.5, sd 0.6) sits at 279.5.

The pooled mix identifies the mean well and the sd weakly: the sd governs between-patient diversity in lesion type, which a pooled share barely constrains. It is taken from the fit here, and is the parameter to revisit when per-participant error mixes with more than 15 items each are available.

What the prior can and cannot fix: it trades word errors for nonwords, so it sets the nonword share. The remaining excess of formal and unrelated errors relative to semantic ones is fixed by the SP model's six-word neighbourhood (two formal and two unrelated competitors against one semantic) and does not move with the prior.

These expected-probability shares ignore item difficulty and realizer fallbacks; `results/engine_validation.md` table 2c is the full-simulation check on the held-out participants.
